agent_research.summary: U.S. rates led the session. Two-year through ten-year yields rose 12 to 14 basis points, the ten-year is back above 5 at 5.1, and those yields sit in the top decile of the past year's levels. SOFR futures still price policy well above cash SOFR of 3.89, after October consumer prices rose 0.4 percent and Fed commentary turned toward another inflation fight. The dollar firmed with that move. Dollar-Canada and dollar-Swiss are near the top of their one-year ranges, while the euro, sterling, the Australian dollar, and the New Zealand dollar weakened. Canada's yields rose with Treasuries. Australia's cash rate and forward path are flat to easier, not the same further-hike path. Euro-area and Japanese long yields barely moved. Brent is 95.82 and WTI is 88.74. Equities are still high and the VIX is 17.5, so this is a rates and dollar story rather than an equity break. Today's U.S. producer prices and the euro-area GDP flash are the next test, with Canada CPI and Japan GDP on Monday.

method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Australia, ECB FX, and CFTC positioning remain packet-level preflight. A stale Canadian benchmark yield stays visible on CA_rates and does not by itself mark the packet stale. CA-dependent expressions and existing-book positions that depend on that leg fail closed. Canadian benchmark freshness uses the Canadian business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks. CME ESR final settlements are collected for research; the €STR curve stays observe_only; Eurex FST3 is not a mark. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.
